The credibility of the evidence in Green vs. National Bank is significantly undermined by the fact that the plaintiff submitted only photocopies of the financial statements. In legal proceedings, particularly those involving financial discrepancies, the best evidence rule generally requires the production of original documents to ensure authenticity and prevent tampering. Since the bank has contested the authenticity of these documents due to the lack of originals for verification, the photocopies are likely to be deemed inadmissible or given little to no weight by the court. Without the original documents to verify their accuracy and integrity, the evidence fails to meet the standard of reliability required to prove the alleged discrepancies in the bank's reported earnings.
